title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-22
notes:
West leads the ♦10 against 4♠. West's diamond lead is won in the dummy. South cashes a top spade on which West discards. West's preempt marks him with a 7 card heart suit almost certainly headed by the ♥A. It looks like South will need the club finesse.

South can guard against West being 0733 with the ♥A and ♣Q without any risk. Dummy's other diamond honour is cashed and a diamond is ruffed. South exits with the ♥4. East can win and does best to return a club. South must win with the ♣A. North's last diamond is ruffed and West is now put on lead with a second heart.

West's best defense is to play another round of hearts. There are many possible successful variations from this point. South can, for example, ruff with the ♠J forcing East to discard as South pitches his ♣J. South can cash the ♣K and play a spade to dummy. East's spades are trump couped at trick 12.
